we have developed a new method that can be used to interpret IncuCyte® ZOOM® assay data to provide estimates for the cell diffusivity D, the proliferation rate λ, and the carrying capacity K, which are key biological parameters that can be used in mathematical models for wound healing.

we have developed a method for estimating cell diffusivity (D) and cell proliferation rate (λ) from IncuCytes ZOOM™ assays by calibrating data from these assays to the Fisher-Kolomogorov model and that we have applied this method to quantify how epidermal growth factors (EGF) affect D and λ in prostate cancer cell lines.
the Fisher-Kolmorogov model is able to accurately predict the dynamics of cell spreading in an in vitro assay.

developing a new approach that can be used to provide a more complete understanding of the cellular-level behaviour driving cell migration.
the development of methods for analysing IncuCyte data that can be used to provide more detailed information about cellular-level behaviour.
developing and applying mathematical models and numerical methods that can be used to interpret data from IncuCyTE™ assays.

we have developed a method to estimate the three parameters D, λ and k of the Fisher-KP model from IncuCytes images.

we have developed a new method for interpreting the IncuCytes ZOOM™ assay, which allows us to quantify the cell motility and proliferation separately, and we demonstrate this method by analysing a suite of Incucyte ZOOM™ assays where EGF is applied in varying doses to PC-3 prostate cell lines.

the proposed method is a novel and useful tool for analysing cell migration and proliferation, and can provide valuable information on the role and effect of different factors on these cellular processes.

our approach provides a method for interpreting IncuCytes ZOOM™ assay that is more informative about the cellular-level mechanisms involved in scratch closure than standard approaches.
we can quantify the role of D, λ, and K, separately, from a single scratch assay.
we provide a method for interpreting IncuCytes ZOOM™ assay results that provides insight into the underlying cell migration and cell division processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use a Fisher-Kolmorgorov model calibrated using data from a standard IncuCyte™ assay to quantify the role cell motility and proliferation play in closing a scratch wound.
the IncuCyter ZOOM™ assay can provide quantitative information about cell motility and proliferation and this information is available from the images alone, without any additional labelling.
it is possible to quantify the balance between cell migration and cell division in a simple way using data from IncuCytes.
